archetypes.name: run-log-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan changes volatile-log commit behavior across driver, docs, constants, and tests, creating high contract-drift risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the proposed volatile-only run-log skip semantics are fully aligned with existing run-log contracts, force-push cleanliness requirements, and documented batch expectations. Check for gaps between the plan's allowlist, the actual publisher outputs, config skip classifications, and tests that prove no dirty or staged paths remain after a skipped flush. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: runtime-floor-sync
archetypes.rationale: Lowering the Python floor to 3.11 spans selectors, packaging, lint/type config, CI, docs, and runtime guards.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the plan accounts for every repo surface that declares, enforces, or assumes the Python runtime floor. Look for mismatches between runtime selector behavior, report-token guards, pyproject metadata, linters, type checkers, CI matrices, and user-facing documentation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cli-fixture-parity
archetypes.rationale: The PR-create fix depends on replacing stubbed JSON behavior with evidence-backed gh CLI behavior and recovery paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the plan's gh pr create changes and tests faithfully model real gh CLI stdout, unsupported flags, conflict recovery, and branch-to-PR resolution timing. Hunt for test-plan holes where stubs could still accept impossible CLI behavior or miss failure-to-resolve cases after successful creation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
